Closed 2026-07-27 after reviewer correction; filed as a security finding in error. Two independent checks confirm it is not a vulnerability. (1) NO GRANT-LIVENESS SIGNAL: _invalid_store_reference is returned from ContextQueries._resolve_store itself, before a _PreparedRemoteStoreResolutionPlan is constructed, so _authorize_remote_store_plan never runs and the use-time snapshot is never captured. The detail therefore cannot distinguish an active grant from a revoked one -- the only thing a security oracle here would need to leak. (2) NO NEW INFORMATION: GET /data-stores?project_id= requires only authorization.require_read (services/data_store_service.py:207) and returns repository.data_stores.list_effective_for_project, i.e. the project's own stores PLUS those inherited from its group. Any caller who can resolve an artifact can already enumerate exactly the effective store names the differing detail would hint at, through the documented API. What remains is at most response-consistency polish -- 'Store artifact reference is invalid.' vs 'Store artifact could not be resolved.' for a caller-supplied malformed locator -- with no confidentiality impact and no roadmap claim. Reopen only if the invalid/unavailable split is deliberately unified as a UX consistency change; tests/test_context_queries_prepared_resolution.py::test_malformed_locator_on_a_granted_store_is_distinguishable_from_denial and the canonicalization suite pin the current contract and would need updating together.

Implemented: 'Undo accept all' next to the Accept all button. Scoped by acceptance_mode==bulk_accepted intersected with the ids this click flipped, so a hand-accept (or a Save edit, which re-stamps human_selected) afterwards removes it from the undo set, and an operation accepted elsewhere while this client was stale is never swept in. Undo PATCHes {status:'proposed'} only, leaving payload and decision note untouched while the server clears the acceptance stamp. Offer is derived, so commit/reload retires it. Partial failure reports how far it got and adopts the server-confirmed state. NOTE: no wall-clock timer - deviation flagged to the user. 19 graph-draft tests (4 proven to fail against naive scoping, 2 against the pre-review version), 206 frontend tests, eslint+ruff clean.

Implemented: useLocalDraft hook + DraftRecoveryNotice, wired into notes, mobile capture, graph-drafts (payload JSON + decision notes), question text, experiment description, project description. Adversarial review found 6 real defects, all fixed: (1) the write effect deleted the draft the recovery effect had just offered, so a reload before Restore lost it permanently; (2) a key change stamped the previous project's text under the new project's key; (3) discard() left on-screen text unprotected; (4) mobile capture stored only the visible one of textNote/hint, so attaching a photo overwrote a long note with a short hint; (5) saving one graph-draft proposal wiped unsaved decision notes on the others (pre-existing, now merges); (6) no sign-out purge, so a shared lab machine offered the previous user's unsent prose. Implemented the a11y floor. (1) prefers-reduced-motion block neutralising animation/transition duration app-wide plus removing the hover-lift transform outright (collapsing duration alone leaves the transform applied). (2) --focus-ring-color/-width/-offset tokens with a global :focus-visible rule. (3) Skip link as first focusable (verified: it IS querySelectorAll's first match) targeting a real <main id=main-content tabindex=-1> landmark. (4) Route change moves focus to main and announces the view via a polite aria-live region, guarded by a ref so re-renders within a view never steal focus, and silent on first render.

FOUND AND FIXED TWO DEFECTS BEYOND THE BEAD: (a) .capture-composer-input:focus set outline:none with higher specificity than the global ring, so the bench capture field gave keyboard users NO indicator - its wrapper's :focus-within glow measures only 1.21:1 and border 2.23:1, both under the 3:1 WCAG asks. Scoped to :not(:focus-visible) so mouse focus keeps the clean look and keyboard focus gets the 6.21:1 ring. (b) I initially pinned the ring to jade-700, which measures 2.32-2.92:1 on dark surfaces - a ring invisible in dark mode. It now points at --accent-text so it flips per theme (5.75-7.23:1 dark). contrast.test.js covers the ring in all three theme blocks and is proven to fail (2.92/2.60) against the pinned version.

Verified in a real browser with genuine keyboard input, not just static assertions: Tab reveals the skip link with a visible ring, and the composer resolves to 2px solid rgb(40,184,150) in dark.
